newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia airport fees raised 10.8 pct - ACCC.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia airport fees raised 10.8 pct - ACCC.

text.p: Anti-monopolies and prices watchdog, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), said on Friday it had approved average airport landing charge increases of 10.8 percent.

The ACCC said the government-owned Federal Airports Corp (FAC) had requested an average price increase of 13.8 percent across its airports, although the increases were planned only at Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide and Perth airports.
"The ACCC has approved an average network increase of 10.8 percent," the ACCC said.

"The ACCC found that operating costs had increased sufficiently to warrant some price increases, but it had some concerns about the approach the FAC had taken to the pricing of these airport services."
It said it was concerned by the loading of all price increases onto the five major airports and the use of the rate of return measure to justify the overall size of the increase.

"The ACCC believes the price increases allow aeronautical operating costs to be substantial recovered and that the airports where the FAC proposes price rises would continue to be profitable," the ACCC said.
Qantas Airways Ltd and Ansett Airlines are the major domestic users of Australia's airports.
Ansett is owned jointly by TNT Ltd and News Corp Ltd, but TNT has said it will sell its 50 percent stake to Air New Zealand Ltd.
